title: Reconciliation and Peace
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Reconciliation and peace means pursuing restored relationship where truth, repentance, wisdom, and love make peace possible. Biblical peace is not pretending nothing is wrong, but seeking right relationship under God.
summary: Reconciliation and peace means pursuing restored relationship where truth, repentance, wisdom, and love make peace possible. Biblical peace is not pretending nothing is wrong, but seeking right relationship under God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reconciles sinners to God and makes peace through His blood. His reconciling work shapes how believers pursue peace with others in truth, humility, and grace.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God is a reconciling God. Through Christ, enemies are brought near and peace is made with God. This Gospel reality shapes the believer’s pursuit of peace with others.

Reconciliation requires truth. False peace that ignores sin, avoids repentance, or hides harm is not biblical peace. God’s peace is joined with righteousness.

Scripture calls believers to pursue peace as far as it depends on them. This acknowledges both responsibility and limitation. A believer can seek peace faithfully without being able to force another person to repent or change.

Peace is especially important in the church because believers share one Lord and one body. The peace of Christ should govern relationships marked by humility, forgiveness, and love.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people avoid reconciliation because pride feels safer. Others are pressured into false reconciliation where repentance and safety are absent. Scripture gives a wise path: pursue peace with truth.

This doctrine helps relationships move beyond silence, bitterness, and surface-level calm toward honest, God-honoring restoration where possible.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pursue peace where God gives opportunity. Confess your own sin, seek forgiveness, speak truth humbly, and desire restoration. Do not confuse peace with denial, and do not use another person’s refusal to repent as an excuse for bitterness in your own heart.
